chunks: From him (al-Layth) from Ibn Abi Umayr from Jamil who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Mudabbir (a slave manumitted upon death), is he sold? He said: If his owner needs his price (money), [then yes]. And he said: If the slave consents, there is no harm.

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah: Title of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.المُدَبَّر: Mudabbir: A slave who is freed upon the death of his master
key_terms.رَضِيَ: Raziya: To consent or be pleased with

ai.seo_question: Can a Mudabbir slave be sold before the owner's death?
ai.summary: In *Al-Istibsar*, Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling where Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a Mudabbir can be sold if the owner requires the funds, but emphasizes that the slave's consent is a key factor for validity. This reflects the Shia juristic view that while the Mudabbir retains a status of conditional freedom, their property rights allow for transferability under specific conditions of need and agreement, distinguishing it from absolute ownership.
